t: Finish Time of Tasks II — Rerooting Tree DP
o:
Each task's finish time is determined bottom-up: a leaf finishes at `baseTime[i]`, while an internal task finishes at `latest + ((latest - earliest) + baseTime[i]) = 2*latest - earliest + baseTime[i]`, where `latest`/`earliest` are the max/min finish times of its children. We must try every node as root and return the smallest root finish time. With $n$ up to $10^5$, recomputing everything per root ($O(n^2)$) is too slow, so we need a rerooting technique: compute all answers with one downward pass and one upward pass over a fixed rooting.

Example 1 (`baseTime=[9,1,5]`): rooting at 1 gives leaf finishes 9 and 5, so node 1 gets `2*9-5+1 = 14`; rooting at 0 gives node 1 = `2*5-9+1 = 2` wait — actually node 1's children from root 0 is only node 2 (finish 5), so node 1 = 6, root 0 = 7; rooting at 2 gives 15. Minimum is 14. Example 2: rooting at 0 gives `2*7-6+4 = 12`. Example 3: the tree is a path, so each root simply accumulates `baseTime` along the chain; rooting at 1 yields 16.
k: The finish-time recurrence simplifies to F(v) = 2*max(child finishes) - min(child finishes) + baseTime[v], and F(leaf) = baseTime[leaf].
Answers fit in 64-bit integers: on a path of 10^5 nodes with baseTime up to 10^5, values reach ~10^10, exceeding 32-bit range.

Rerooting works because when the root moves from u to a neighbor v, only v's child set changes: it gains u, whose finish time is computable from u's data excluding v (keep top-2 max and top-2 min of children).
Use iterative DFS to avoid stack overflow at n = 10^5.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force over All Roots
a.i: For every candidate root, run a fresh DFS computing finish times bottom-up and record the root's finish time. This directly implements the definition and is easy to verify, but costs $O(n)$ per root for $O(n^2)$ total — acceptable only for tiny inputs, serving as a correctness baseline.
s: For each node r in 0..n-1, run an iterative DFS from r collecting nodes in visit order.
Process nodes in reverse visit order: leaves get baseTime, internal nodes get 2*max - min + baseTime over their children's finishes.
Answer is the minimum root finish time over all r.
a.t: O(n^2) — one full O(n) DFS per candidate root.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency list, parent array, and per-root buffers.

a.i: Root the tree at node 0 and compute F(v) bottom-up. When the root moves from u to its child v, v gains exactly one new child: u. The finish time of u in this new orientation depends only on u's other children's finishes plus nothing from v, so we precompute an 'up' value per node. To exclude a specific child when taking max/min, keep the top-two maximums and top-two minimums of children finishes at every node. Each node's answer as root combines its own children's finishes with its up value.
s: Root at 0; get a DFS visit order and parents iteratively.
Reverse-order pass: for each v compute F(v), plus mx1/mx2 (two largest child finishes) and mn1/mn2 (two smallest), remembering which child attains mx1 and mn1.

Forward-order pass: for each edge u->child w, collect candidate finishes {up(u)} plus u's children finishes excluding w (pick mx2 instead of mx1 if w holds mx1; same for min). up(w) = 2*max - min + baseTime[u], or baseTime[u] if no candidates.
Final pass: for each v, answer-as-root = combine(children finishes of v together with up(v)) using the same formula; take the global minimum.
a.t: O(n) — three linear passes over the tree (post-order, pre-order, final scan); each edge is processed a constant number of times.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency list plus constant-size auxiliary arrays per node.

w: In an interview, present the brute force briefly to establish the recurrence, then move straight to rerooting — it is the expected solution for Hard tree problems with 'choose any root'. Pitfalls: (1) forgetting that single-child nodes have latest == earliest, so the (latest - earliest) term vanishes — the general formula handles this automatically; (2) using 32-bit integers, which overflow on long paths; (3) recursive DFS overflowing the call stack at n = 10^5 — always iterate; (4) incorrectly excluding the child being re-rooted into when computing up values — you must keep top-two max/min, not just top-one. Edge cases: n = 1 (answer is baseTime[0]), star graphs (center vs. leaf roots differ greatly), and paths. Follow-ups might ask for the argmin root, handling updates to baseTime, or generalizing to DAGs/forests.
